motivation.problems: Data engineers and analytics engineers repair pipelines and libraries after an upstream feed changes its shape. In these tasks a vendor or connector changes format and the next run produces wrong data without failing. Fivetran or Stripe exports start resending changed records, so dbt models show duplicates and stale totals (pdk-dbt-stripe-dbt, pdk-dbt-hubspot-dbt). Files change encoding or layout: a sep= line in CSV (pdk-clevercsv-etl), CONTINUE records in XLS (pdk-xlrd-etl), locale formats in sheets (pdk-gspread-pandas-etl), new Parquet types (pdk-diffly-dataframe). Incremental loaders mis-track state when a schema changes mid-run or a site is added (pdk-target-csv-etl, pdk-tap-weatherapi-etl, pdk-graflo-pipeline). Nightly ordering and failure handling go wrong (pdk-yato-pipeline). Each report also expects results to be the same on reruns and no regression in existing tests.
motivation.how_tasks_exemplify: Each task is a public repository checked out at a pinned commit in /app, with a Python virtual environment in /opt/venv and, where needed, dbt and DuckDB. Sample inputs such as CSV, Parquet, XML, SQLite files or seeds are copied to /data or sit in the project. The agent has no network access. The prompt gives the symptom and the required behavior, but no pointer to the faulty code. After the agent finishes, a separate verifier applies the agent's diff of /app, adds hidden tests, runs the repository's own checks and the hidden suite as an unprivileged user, and grades both reports. Some prompts add lint, type or changelog requirements (pdk-databallpy-dataframe, pdk-schwifty-etl, pdk-etlplus-pipeline).
prompt_patterns: A first person production symptom after a vendor or connector change, with a sample location in /data (pdk-dbt-stripe-dbt).
A behavior spec in prose with edge cases, defaults and idempotence rules, ending with a request to fix the library without breaking existing tests (pdk-sayn-pipeline).
An opt-in feature request for a parser or loader, with defaults that must not change (pdk-xmltodict-etl, pdk-glom-etl).
A format or locale decoding failure where every sample file must read exactly as written (pdk-xlrd-etl, pdk-gspread-pandas-etl).
A dbt project fix that must stay in SQL models, macros and YAML and pass dbt build (pdk-dbt-openai-dbt, pdk-dbt-unirate-dbt).
open_questions: The brief names two roles, but one showcase task has the category Sports analytics and another Payments and banking. Is the catalog meant to include them under data engineering?
Two sampled tasks (pdk-pyparsing-etl, pdk-agate-excel-etl) have empty instruction text in the tasks file. Is that a data export error?
Which Python process user and privileges does the agent have at run time? Dockerfiles mention an unprivileged user dpapp for the verifier, but the agent's user is not stated in the files I read.
The pdk-dbt-opentelemetry-dbt Dockerfile starts with template comments (FILL markers). Are these comments leftovers, and does the task have no /data sample folder?
What are the reward and pass criteria in grader.py (number of hidden tests, weighting between repo checks and hidden suite)? I did not describe them.
